expected.summary: Fourteen minutes before the anchor the data-platform team upgraded users-db, the Postgres behind user-profile, from PostgreSQL 14.11 to 16.4 by blue/green switchover (DBA-3410). Every user-profile pod logged its users-db pool re-established against server_version 16.4 within seconds. pg_upgrade does not carry planner statistics over and nobody ran ANALYZE on the new cluster, so the profile lookup that joins users to user_preferences now plans a sequential scan: user-profile's pg.select spans on users-db went from about 6 ms to a p95 of about 800 ms in one step, and user-profile logs slow query warnings naming users-db. user-profile returns no errors and its version did not change. About four in ten GET /profile requests take longer than the 500 ms timeout web-bff and mobile-bff set on user-profile and fail with 504; every other route is healthy. The failures propagate through web-bff and mobile-bff to edge-gateway, where the alert fires. review's 2.2.0 rollout, finished nine minutes before onset, is unrelated: review is an optional call on product pages and stayed error-free.
contributingFactors: the PostgreSQL 14 to 16 upgrade of users-db (DBA-3410) leaving the new cluster without planner statistics
no ANALYZE run after the switchover, so the profile lookup plans a sequential scan until autovacuum analyzes users
web-bff and mobile-bff giving user-profile a 500 ms budget

criteria.description: Does the brief name the users-db upgrade to PostgreSQL 16 (DBA-3410) as the origin, with the new cluster lacking planner statistics so user-profile's lookups slowed past the BFFs' 500 ms timeout on GET /profile and the failures reached edge-gateway? 5 = the upgrade, the missing statistics or bad plan, the slow users-db reads and the victim chain. Saying only 'users-db is slow' scores at most 2.

Is it grounded in user-profile's pg.select spans on users-db stepping up at the switchover, the pool re-established logs naming server_version 16.4, the slow query warnings, and the BFF 504s on user-profile? Cap at 3 unless it ties the slowdown to the moment of the switchover.
Does it avoid blaming review's 2.2.0 rollout, a user-profile code change, traffic or edge-gateway, and avoid claiming user-profile returned errors of its own?
Concise, structured, no filler or speculation.
